% ============================================================
% Spider Auction grid puzzle - ASP (clingo) encoding
% ============================================================

% ---- Domains ----
prices(45;60;75;90).
winners(charles;freddie;shelley;vicky).
spiders(archaenido;cart_spider;darkback;whip_spider).

% ---- Assignment: each price gets exactly one winner, and vice versa ----
1 { assign_winner(P,W) : winners(W) } 1 :- prices(P).
1 { assign_winner(P,W) : prices(P) } 1 :- winners(W).

% ---- Assignment: each price gets exactly one spider, and vice versa ----
1 { assign_spider(P,S) : spiders(S) } 1 :- prices(P).
1 { assign_spider(P,S) : prices(P) } 1 :- spiders(S).

% ============================================================
% Clues
% ============================================================

% Clue 1: Freddie's purchase cost 15 dollars more than the cart spider.
% Find the price Freddie paid (P_freddie) and the price of the cart spider (P_cart).
% Then P_freddie must be P_cart + 15.
:- assign_winner(P_freddie, freddie),
   assign_spider(P_cart, cart_spider),
   P_freddie != P_cart + 15.

% Clue 2: Of the darkback and the cart spider, one sold for $60 and the other was won by Vicky.
% This means:
% (darkback sold for $60 AND cart_spider was Vicky's purchase) OR
% (cart_spider sold for $60 AND darkback was Vicky's purchase)
% We need to ensure that at least one of these two scenarios is true.
scenario2_option1 :- assign_spider(60, darkback), assign_winner(P_vicky, vicky), assign_spider(P_vicky, cart_spider).
scenario2_option2 :- assign_spider(60, cart_spider), assign_winner(P_vicky, vicky), assign_spider(P_vicky, darkback).
:- not scenario2_option1, not scenario2_option2.

% Clue 3: Of the spider that sold for $75 and Shelley's purchase, one was the archaenido and the other was the cart spider.
% This means:
% (archaenido sold for $75 AND cart_spider was Shelley's purchase) OR
% (cart_spider sold for $75 AND archaenido was Shelley's purchase)
% We need to ensure that at least one of these two scenarios is true.
scenario3_option1 :- assign_spider(75, archaenido), assign_winner(P_shelley, shelley), assign_spider(P_shelley, cart_spider).
scenario3_option2 :- assign_spider(75, cart_spider), assign_winner(P_shelley, shelley), assign_spider(P_shelley, archaenido).
:- not scenario3_option1, not scenario3_option2.

% Clue 4: The arachnid that sold for $90 was either Shelley's purchase or the darkback.
% Find the spider that sold for $90 (S_ninety) and the spider Shelley bought (S_shelley).
% S_ninety must be equal to S_shelley OR S_ninety must be darkback.
:- assign_spider(90, S_ninety),
   assign_winner(P_shelley, shelley),
   assign_spider(P_shelley, S_shelley),
   S_ninety != S_shelley,
   S_ninety != darkback.

% ============================================================
% Output
% ============================================================
#show assign_winner/2.
#show assign_spider/2.

% Define price differences for clues
% price_diff(P1, P2, D) means P1 is D dollars more than P2
price_diff(p25_99, p24_99, 1).
price_diff(p26_99, p25_99, 1).
price_diff(p27_99, p26_99, 1).

price_diff(p26_99, p24_99, 2).
price_diff(p27_99, p25_99, 2).

% ---- Assignment: each price gets exactly one name, and vice versa ----
1 { name(P,N) : names(N) } 1 :- prices(P).
1 { name(P,N) : prices(P) } 1 :- names(N).

% ---- Assignment: each price gets exactly one wine, and vice versa ----
1 { wine(P,W) : wines(W) } 1 :- prices(P).
1 { wine(P,W) : prices(P) } 1 :- wines(W).

% ---- Assignment: each price gets exactly one entree, and vice versa ----
1 { entree(P,E) : entrees(E) } 1 :- prices(P).
1 { entree(P,E) : prices(P) } 1 :- entrees(E).

% ============================================================
% Clues
% ============================================================

% Clue 1: Lynda paid 2 dollars more than the diner who ordered the beef stir-fry.
:- name(P1, lynda), entree(P2, beef_stir_fry), not price_diff(P1, P2, 2).

% Clue 2: The diner who ordered the beef stir-fry was either the one who had the merlot or the one who had the bordeaux.
:- entree(P, beef_stir_fry), not wine(P, merlot), not wine(P, bordeaux).

% Clue 3: The person who paid $26.99 didn't have the zinfandel.
:- wine(p26_99, zinfandel).

% Clue 4: The one who had the chianti paid 2 dollars less than the diner who ordered the filet mignon.
% This means the filet mignon diner paid 2 dollars more than the chianti diner.
:- wine(P1, chianti), entree(P2, filet_mignon), not price_diff(P2, P1, 2).

% Clue 5: Of the one who had the merlot and the one who had the chianti,
%         one paid $25.99 and the other ordered the lobster tail.
% Helper predicates for the two possibilities
clue5_possibility_1(P_merlot, P_chianti) :- P_merlot = p25_99, entree(P_chianti, lobster_tail).
clue5_possibility_2(P_merlot, P_chianti) :- P_chianti = p25_99, entree(P_merlot, lobster_tail).

% Constraint: one of the possibilities must be true
:- wine(P_merlot, merlot), wine(P_chianti, chianti), P_merlot != P_chianti,
   not clue5_possibility_1(P_merlot, P_chianti),
   not clue5_possibility_2(P_merlot, P_chianti).

% Clue 6: The diner who ordered the beef stir-fry paid 1 dollar more than Frances.
:- entree(P1, beef_stir_fry), name(P2, frances), not price_diff(P1, P2, 1).

% Clue 7: Neither Willie nor the diner who ordered the beef stir-fry was the person who paid $27.99.
:- name(p27_99, willie).
:- entree(p27_99, beef_stir_fry). 
:- name(P, willie), entree(P, beef_stir_fry).

% ============================================================
% Output
% ============================================================
#show name/2.
#show wine/2.
#show entree/2.
